CCP – Cuneiform Commentaries Project (Yale)

  • Site: https://ccp.yale.edu (E. Frahm, E. Jiménez, M. Frazer, K. Wagensonner, 2013–2026).
  • Retrieved: 2026-10-19 (saved HTML pages, a text extraction next to each).
  • License / copyright: "© Cuneiform Commentaries Project"; no open licence stated (the footer says "Copyright © 2026 Yale University · All rights reserved"). Treated as copyrighted: the pages and extractions are gitignored; only this README is committed. Quote briefly with attribution, citing the DOI given on each page.

Contents

Folder What
1.3--P394923--Ludlul-commentary/ CCP 1.3, the Nineveh commentary on Ludlul (K 3291, mukallimtu), ed. A. Lenzi (2015), rev. E. Jiménez: introduction, transliteration, translation, notes. eBL quotes the same tablet as NinNAQuo2. DOI 10079/cc2frb2.
1.4--P404917--Theodicy-commentary/ CCP 1.4, the Babylonian commentary on the Theodicy (BM 66882+, from Borsippa), ed. E. Jiménez (2017): introduction, transliteration, translation, notes. DOI 10079/7m0cg9h. (eBL's Theodicy ATF quotes the same tablet as BabaLBCom1.)

Usefulness

Rank 4: the ancient scholars' own explanations of rare words of the two poems ("X = Y"), a window onto how Babylonian scholars read these texts (guidelines §1, second purpose). Use them in the apparatus where a line's rare word is explained by the ancient commentary.
